10. The smaller decisive experiment

The specified smaller experiment is a 0.5 m-long loaded bay between two anchored crossframes, using six field bars, two spare bar bodies and twenty cartridges. It uses the actual capture head, three pump branches, finite wafer stock, temporary holder, independent metrology and restrained restoration rack.

It targets 200 physical operations and twelve recoveries. It does not substitute for the full 2.3 m, three-geometry, 1,000-operation service.

The complete estimate is $324,815, including the separate campaign. Major build entries include:

Experimental subsystem	Estimate
First capture/cutter/die/pullback assembly	$38,000
Three pumps plus branch hardware	$22,760
Small positioner, ground shoring, independent pad stages and dampers	$98,000
Finger, lift and stiffness upgrades	$11,000
Bay stock, prototype wafers and backup cage	$29,000
Depot, saddles and changer	$15,200
Controls, independent metrology, fault fixtures and test access	$35,000
Mechanical preparation, programming and transport	$63,000

The campaign separately pays observers, pre/post inspection, matched-control operation, laboratory access, consumables, process electricity, facility electricity, waste and transport.

The decisive sequence must:

Carry the actual 100 N equipment load with tools withdrawn.
Introduce a failed second-end engagement with 0.5–2.5 kN internal opposing load and near-zero outer resultant.
Reject a sensor-looking false seat using its own observations.
Capture the complete internal force path.
Experience a partly completed cut, active pump failure and bad standby.
Complete outer isolation and prove actual gaps.
Transfer the contained energy to the rack.
Restore from finite stock.
Finish with useful load supported and every construction tool withdrawn.

Independent measurements must record support reactions, both pad wrenches, pin/shank strain, cage and return-tie forces, pressure/flow, local cutting travel, both outer gaps, displacement, electricity, oil state, debris and stock.

This experiment could establish the manufactured local operation. It would not establish full-size access, all fault combinations, long life, production yield, or the required economic advantage.

source_excerpts.text:
11. What remains unresolved

The work now has a finite construction family, an explicit contained-jam removal mechanism, supported static prefixes, staged force attribution, observable holder calibration, finite cartridge restoration and substantially improved exterior routes.

It still lacks:

A complete cut-transient and intact-connection strength certificate across the admitted physical range.
Manufactured cutter, cage, keeper, damper and actuator response maps.
Closure of the conservative final holder-plus-rail deflection margin.
Complete own-port transient access and the four-face inspection route.
Qualified cradle, saddle and rack-release observations.
Physical execution of the reference service.
A consequential matched economic advantage.

Scaling to ten or one hundred times as many parts would additionally require new support layouts, rails, depots, foundations, calibration strategies and fault-stock policies. It cannot preserve the present gravity, travel or computation costs by assumption.

The supported result is a more explicit candidate and an executable account of why it is not yet the requested invention. The captured internal-load boundary is worth preserving as an engineering principle. The current complete installation cannot honestly be called economical, fully load-safe across its admitted recovery envelope, or physically autonomous on the evidence obtained here.
